transcript.text: What is the main thing the tumble dryer is doing wrong?
lights come on but nothing happens when I press start, drum doesn't turn. It's a Hotpoint condenser dryer

Please start a programme on your Hotpoint tumble dryer and listen for a few seconds. It is vital that you just listen; do not open the door or reach in while it is running. Can you hear the motor humming or running even though the drum doesn't turn, or is it silent?
Silent, no sound at all when I press start.

Thanks for letting me know about the lack of motor sound. An overloaded drum, or even just one large heavy item like a duvet or rug, can sometimes prevent the drum from turning properly. Was it overloaded or a single bulky item (and have you taken some out), or was it a normal load?
Normal load, nothing heavy. The door has felt loose for a few days though and now it won't click shut.

Thanks for letting us know about the door issue. Please ensure you do not force the door open or shut, and never attempt to force or bypass the door lock. To proceed, please follow these steps: 1. Open the door. 2. Check that no clothing is caught in it. 3. Shut it firmly until it clicks. 4. Press start. Does it still show the door as open?
No click when I shut it, the door swings back slightly open. The plastic tongue on the door has snapped off, found the piece on the floor. It only starts if I hold the door shut.

To match the right part for your dryer I need its exact model. Could you send me the model number? It's on the rating plate inside the door rim or on the back — a photo is fine.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
I don't know it offhand. I'll look inside the door recess and see if I can read it. One sec.

To match the right part for your dryer I need its exact model. Could you send me the model number? It's on the rating plate inside the door rim or on the back — a photo is fine.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
Still looking for it, haven't found the sticker yet. Is there anything else I should check meanwhile?

[Heading: Door latch / switch]
Thanks for letting me know about the model number issue. Based on your description, the door catch or interlock is the most likely cause of the problem, although it would need testing to be certain. Since I cannot check whether a suitable replacement is available without the specific model details, having an appliance engineer attend is the best next step to resolve this safely and effectively.
